answer: Gate influence behind a single hash-linked work ridge: each identity must extend it every epoch with a signed output that commits to the prior entry. Voting weight and emission share stay near zero until the ridge is long enough and densely attested by established peers. Like drainage in karst terrain, only one continuous path counts; parallel stubs or a reused cipher of earlier work are treated as clones and freeze weight. A sybil must therefore keep a separate live ridge for every fake, so cost scales with identities and elapsed epochs, not with cheap mass signup.
